sections.title: Market Pulse: Indices Decline Amid Inflation, Oil Price Concerns

items.headline: U.S. Equities Close Lower as Geopolitical Tensions Fuel Oil Rally and Rate Hike Expectations
items.summary: Major U.S. stock indices ended Wednesday's session in negative territory, driven by persistent inflation concerns, escalating oil prices spurred by U.S.-Iran tensions, and a hawkish outlook on interest rates. The S&P 500, NASDAQ, and Dow Jones Industrial Average all registered declines. The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) also saw an uptick, reflecting heightened market unease. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Turn Therapeutics Surges on Strong Performance
items.summary: Turn Therapeutics saw a significant surge in its stock price, making it one of the top gainers of the day.

items.headline: Marvell Technology Up on Raised Revenue Targets
items.summary: Marvell Technology rallied after its CEO delivered an upward revision to the company's fiscal 2027 and 2028 revenue targets.

items.headline: Meta Platforms Rises with New AI Agent Launch
items.summary: Meta Platforms gained ground following the launch of Muse, its new artificial intelligence personal agent.

items.headline: Amgen Plunges on Trial Failure News
items.summary: Amgen Inc. was a major decliner in the Dow, with its stock falling significantly after a late-stage trial for a drug failed, impacting the pharmaceutical sector.

items.headline: Casey's General Stores Tumbles on Disappointing Sales
items.summary: Casey's General Stores experienced a sharp drop in share price after reporting disappointing same-store sales growth and maintaining its full-year outlook.

items.headline: Dyne Therapeutics Sees Significant Decline
items.summary: Dyne Therapeutics was among the day's biggest losers, experiencing a notable drop in its stock value.

items.headline: Energy Sector Leads as Others Lag; AI Driving Tech Gains
items.summary: The Energy Select Sector SPDR ($XLE) was the only broad sector to gain, rising 1%, fueled by surging oil prices. In contrast, Financials ($XLF) fell 1.4%, Health Care ($XLV) declined 2.6%, and Materials ($XLB) dropped 0.9%, indicating broad weakness across several key areas of the market. AI-related demand continues to be a strong theme, benefiting companies like Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which reported strong earnings driven by AI-optimized servers. Industrials were noted as a relatively weaker sector.

items.headline: Fed's Stance and Upcoming Inflation Data Eyed by Investors
items.summary: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to hold interest rates steady at its September 15-16 meeting, though a Reuters poll indicates a growing number of analysts anticipate at least one hike this year. The CME FedWatch Tool currently shows a 60.4% chance of a 25-basis-point rate increase. Investors are keenly awaiting the August Producer Price Index (PPI) and Consumer Price Index (CPI) reports later this week, which are crucial for shaping future interest rate expectations. Additionally, mortgage rates have climbed to their highest level since June 2025, reaching 6.85% for a 30-year fixed-rate. The Minneapolis Fed also noted that more tariff costs are being passed to consumers and that the AI boom is contributing to inflation.

items.headline: U.S.-Iran Tensions Drive Oil Prices Higher, Adding to Market Pressure
items.summary: Renewed fighting between the U.S. and Iran pushed crude oil prices above $100 per barrel, with Brent crude nearing $99.50. These geopolitical developments are a significant factor in the broader market decline, exacerbating inflation concerns and influencing central bank policy expectations.

items.headline: Key Earnings Reports and Corporate Developments
items.summary: Beyond major movers like Casey's General Stores, several companies reported earnings today. SailPoint Inc. ($SAIL), Core & Main Inc. ($CNM), Chewy Inc. ($CHWY), and J. Jill Inc. ($JILL) were among those scheduled to release results. AeroVironment ($AVAV) is also set to report Q3 earnings, with analysts anticipating strong performance driven by recent contract wins. Separately, Google announced a substantial €13 billion investment in AI infrastructure in Finland over the next two years.
